Slides and video recording of the presentation given by Marian Clemens Manz (Digital Humanities Lab, University of Basel) at DaSCHCon on IIIF, 3D & Interoperability on Wednesday 25 October 2023. The talk looks at the past, present and future of 3D documentation of cultural heritage. It reviews how 3D documentation has developed, assesses current methods and their challenges, and outlines future directions such as more standardized workflows, better surface textures and deep learning to reconstruct damaged artefacts. Using an object from the Historisches Museum Basel ("Digitales Schaudepot") as its starting point, the talk draws on models of holistic data management and semantic interoperability. It then presents a structure for preserving 3D data in six largely iterative components, an approach to collecting standards and tools, and a high-level recommended workflow. It ends with perspectives on testing 3D in the IIIF Presentation API and joining the community discussions around Linked Open Usable Data. The presentation is based on the paper "Recommended 3D Workflow for Digital Heritage Practices" (https://doi.org/10.2352/issn.2168-3204.2023.20.1.5).

## Learning outcomes

After working through this resource, users will be able to:

- outline how 3D documentation of cultural heritage has developed and the challenges it faces today
- describe the components of a recommended workflow for 3D digitization and data preservation
- explain why standardization and interoperability (e.g. IIIF, LOUD) matter for the reuse of 3D data
- find the paper this recommended workflow is based on
